findings.title: Keep Watch's start card and a critical tail's card name a Spectator's token as someone in the room - a dead student's watcher among them, under the dead student's name
findings.where: scripts/watch-gm.mjs:83-94 (namesIn), 106-109; scripts/tail-gm.mjs:98-109 (standingIn), 132-136; against scripts/movement.mjs:3761-3772 (countsAsPresent); scripts/spectator-dead.mjs:186-205; scripts/visibility.mjs:539-543
findings.what_happens: Both lists of who stands in a room skip a Monokuma, the dead as the GMs hold them and a hidden token, and nothing else. A Spectator is a character with the spectator flag and an unhidden token that walks free and is shown to its owner alone. Since E62 C3b every student who dies - a death the GMs keep included - gets a watcher actor named after the student, flagged spectator, with an unhidden token where the body lies; that actor is not itself dead (the death is on the student's id), so isDeadForGm is false for it. namesIn and standingIn therefore name the watcher - by the dead student's name - and any E92 Spectator, where movement.mjs's one answer (no Monokuma, no Spectator, no dead, no hidden) leaves them out. CHAINS.md B-R7 fixed this for the door cards and the breach's ('the door cards reached a Spectator'); these two lists were not in its scope.
findings.failure_scenario: Sayaka is killed and the GMs keep the death; her player's watcher walks into the gym; at the next Eclipse's start Kyoko, keeping watch over the gym, is told 'You see Sayaka there' while her map shows nobody - a dead student reported standing in a room, from a token her browser does not draw.
findings.expected: One answer for who is in a room, as R7163 states it: 'for every card a room's people are sent' - countsAsPresent (or its rule) in namesIn and standingIn.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a Spectator test in both functions and their callers: none. Checked that the watcher is not caught as dead: the flag is on the new actor only (spectator-dead.mjs:12-13), isDeadForGm reads the actor's own record (settings.mjs:3817-3819). Checked hidden: the watcher's token is created hidden:false (spectator-dead.mjs:202) and hidden only by the module's visibility. R7163 (tests-tier0.mjs:25990) holds tellRooms and tellBreach only; R6403 (tests-tier1.mjs:38712) reads only that the two sites join with listOf; R6023 is Echoes. The live crossing cards of a watch are not touched: a Spectator records no crossing (movement.mjs:3030-3032), so CROSSING_SETTLED never names one. Echoes is not touched: echoCounts refuses the spectator flag (echoes-gm.mjs:59).

findings.title: The Students window's State list publishes a kept death and destroys its Truth Bullets, where the window's note and the code's own note say the list is a quiet repair that keeps the inventory
findings.what_happens: On a 'Dead, not found' row (a death the GMs keep) the State list offers Alive, Dead, not found, Dead and Monocub. Dead and Monocub both run makeKnown -> publishDeath, which destroys the victim's Truth Bullets (unless the kill kept them), writes the death to the world, tells whoever held a copy and publishes the crime's ties. The window's note says 'The State column fixes a mis-click. The change is saved when you press Apply, with no announcement' and places 'a death destroys Truth Bullets' under the row's buttons; the note in applyAliveStates says 'Dying through the DROPDOWN keeps the inventory AND stays quiet (F16)'. The publish itself is the owner's decision (Q3, recorded at 509-510 and 623-625); what the GM is told is not.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM sees 'Dead, not found' on Sayaka's row and picks Dead to tidy the list before a session; on Apply the death is the table's and the Truth Bullets she carried are gone, which the note above the table said only the row's buttons do.
findings.expected: The note (and the code comment) say that Dead or Monocub on a 'Dead, not found' row makes the death known as the discovery does, Truth Bullets included.
findings.refutation_tried: Read publishDeath whole: it is the discovery's road (death.mjs:502-520) and destroys bullets unless keepBullets. Checked that the unfound option exists only on such rows (gm-students.mjs:134) and that the publish is a recorded decision (gm-students.mjs:509-510, 623-625: 'its record, its Truth Bullets and its row go as the discovery takes them') - so the behaviour stands as a decision and only the two texts are the finding.

findings.title: Echoes counts a character marked Not in the class that a player owns as a living student of another player
findings.what_happens: echoCounts refuses a body, a hidden token, a Monokuma, a Monocub, a Spectator and a character no player owns, and nothing else: a character carrying notInClass - not a student by studentActors' rule - counts when a player other than the asker owns it.
findings.failure_scenario: A player owns a guest character the GM marked Not in the class, standing in the kitchen; another player's Echoes answers 'the kitchen' though no student stands there.
findings.expected: The header's 'a living student of another player': the student roster's rule, notInClass refused as well.
findings.refutation_tried: R6023 (tests-tier1.mjs:59049-59064) feeds a body, Monokuma, Monocub, Spectator, hidden, no owner, own player and a non-character, no notInClass case. The flag is the GMs' to write (gm-students.mjs:228-236, the audit's GM_FLAGS), so a player cannot add or keep it. How often a player owns such a character is not known; hence nit.

findings.title: The GM panel's standing block is rebuilt on every actor, item and token write in the world, and each Daily Life build walks the whole season checklist
findings.where: scripts/gm-panel.mjs:653-658 (watch: actors, items, tokens, two stores and every module world setting), 975-980 (firstOutstandingStep with no list), 912-929 (keyPlanStatus in an Investigation); scripts/season-setup.mjs:268-300, 745; scripts/fog-diagnostics.mjs:845-905; scripts/gm-students.mjs:571-577 (the Students table, the same on every actor write)
findings.what_happens: keepLive coalesces the writes (120 ms, config.mjs:439) and then builds the block: in Daily Life nextStep falls through to firstOutstandingStep(), whose default runs steps({ roomScene: homeScene() }) - about twenty rows over the roster, the room census, the area sum over every room piece of the school and namedRegions of every scene; in an Investigation keyPlanStatus walks every scene's traces. A player's every step is an updateToken, and a Daggerheart roll writes its actor several times. fog-diagnostics.mjs:855-858 already notes the area sum 'is read on every redraw of the GM panel'. The Students window rebuilds its whole table (a sheetMode and a standingOffers per row) on the same actor writes.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM keeps the panel open through a busy Daily Life; each settled step of any of five players rebuilds the block and the checklist on the GM's browser - how much frame time that takes was not measured.
findings.expected: Measured once (perf()'s `live..drpg-gmp-standing` sample, perf-timings.mjs) before deciding; the checklist's answer could be kept until a setting or a roster change.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that the branch is the ordinary one: an incident, a round, an Eclipse, a stopped end, a trial, a held body and a waiting body all return earlier (gm-panel.mjs:819-967), so a plain Daily Life reaches 977. Scenario 86 (frame work) does not open the panel (its source names no panel region), so no count of this exists. The cost is unmeasured: severity nit, not more.
findings.live_check: new live check: perf() at a table, GM panel open in Daily Life, four players walking for a minute; read the `live..drpg-gmp-standing` sample count and its middle time.

findings.title: The GM panel forgets which sections the GM unfolded every time a tile brings it back
findings.where: scripts/gm-panel.mjs:474-489 (open from the phase alone), 599-619 (close, run, openGmPanel anew); lang/en.json DRPG.Tips.Sweep.Gm.panelSectionTooltip
findings.what_happens: Every tile closes the panel, runs, and opens a new panel; buildSections opens a section only by the phase (`inSeason && !section.collapsed`), and keepLive carries folds only across a rebuild inside one window. So Between sessions and Diagnostics, collapsed by default, fold again after each tile pressed in them.
findings.failure_scenario: Between sessions a GM opens Between sessions, presses Room Setup, closes it, and the panel returns with the section folded; each further tile there costs the unfold again.
findings.expected: The panel reopened by a tile opens the sections it closed with.
findings.refutation_tried: Searched buildSections and openGmPanel for a kept fold (a variable, a client setting, localStorage): none. The tooltip says the panel keeps the choice 'while it stays open', which is true and is the limit of it; no decision records the reset after a tile.

findings.title: Despair Flow's Split evenly rewrites every student's assignment at once, without a question, in a window whose other changes wait for Save
findings.what_happens: Split evenly answers the window, autoAssign writes a new map at once (every student but those set to '- nobody -', in name order) and the window opens again. Picks made earlier and saved are replaced; Cancel afterwards undoes nothing. Revoke asks first because 'every other destruction in this module asks first' (97-98); this one does not.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM with a hand-made split of eight students presses Split evenly on the Students tab to see what it would do, then Cancel: the hand-made split is gone.
findings.expected: A question before the write, Cancel the default, as Revoke has; or the split drawn into the selects for Save to write.
findings.refutation_tried: The TEAM-01 note (38-48) records that the three buttons act at once and that the assignments are rebuilt, not that Split evenly needs no question; autoAssign keeps only '- nobody -' rows (assignments.mjs:145-147).

recipe: 1. GM opens the GM panel in Daily Life with the season set up.
2. Four players walk their tokens for one minute.
3. GM runs game.drpg.perf() and reads the live..drpg-gmp-standing line.
l1.settles_if: A middle time under a few ms and a count near the number of settled steps: nit stands or falls to none; tens of ms: perf minor.

not_established.what: A tail of a target who does not cross while an incident runs is not ended by the incident (tail-gm.mjs:87-92 is asked only at the target's settled crossing, 124), and goes on once the incident closes until a body is announced or the day ends. Whether the rule ('Silent: ... an incident running', tail-gm.mjs:26-27) means 'ends' or 'sends nothing while' is a question for the owner, not settled from source.

Whether an incident's start ends an eavesdrop at once: nothing in eavesdrop-gm.mjs hears the incident (325 lists the time of day, the Eclipse, the phase and the deaths); the end comes from the voice pass's sweep (listensInForce, 182-189), whose trigger by the incident's write (voice.mjs RECONCILE_HOOKS) was not traced. A harness probe with one eavesdrop and an incident opened would settle it.

The microphone block's lift after an eavesdrop ends is a setTimeout in the primary's page (eavesdrop-gm.mjs:154); a primary that reloads inside EAVESDROP_GRACE_MS leaves the block until the next settle. How soon that settle comes at a table was not measured (LIVE-E69-03 reads the grace itself).
